newsitem.title: USA: USAF OKs commercial Delta rocket launch resumption.
newsitem.headline: USAF OKs commercial Delta rocket launch resumption.

text.p: The U.S. Air Force Space Command said it approved resuming commercial Delta-2 rocket launches by McDonnell Douglas Corp from Vandenberg Air Force Base, Calif, and Cape Canaveral Air Station in Florida.
Friday's commercial space launch of a Delta is now set to carry five IRIDIUM satellites for cellular telephone communications into space from Vandenberg at 0812 Pacific time (1512 GMT).
A second Delta-2 launch, that one from Cape Canaveral on May 11, is scheduled to carry a Norweigan Thor-2A communications satellite into space.

The approval followed an analysis in the wake of the failure of a Delta-2 shortly after launch from Cape Canaveral Air Station on January 17. That rocket was carrying an Air Force global positioning satellite.
The Air Force Space Command, located at Colorado Springs, Colo., said that "McDonnell Douglas and its contractor team have taken numerous actions for a safe return to flight."
"Based on its review and the actions the Air Force and the contractor team have taken, the Air Force is confident the Delta-2 can return to flight," the space command said in a statement.
